OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form; spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped, a leading '+' and country
            code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The stored value is a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits and is returned in that form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, permits creating this owner even though another owner
            already has the same last name and address (they knowingly share a household).
            Write-only hint used only on create; it is never stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'

          properties:
            id:
              title: ID

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a global 4-digit
                zero-padded sequence assigned at creation.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature end-to-end, keeping each concern in its own small unit.

**What the feature does:** When `POST /api/owners` is called with `sharesHousehold: true` and the new owner matches an existing owner's household (same last name + address, compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), creation is allowed and the new owner plus every existing household member are stamped with the same stable `householdId`, which is now returned on `GET`. Without the flag, a matching household is still rejected with `DuplicateHouseholdException` as before.

**Changes:**

- **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` schema (regenerates `OwnerDto`).
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added the `household_id` column mapping with getter/setter (and to `toString`).
- **DB schemas** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `household_id` column.
- **`validation/HouseholdKey.java`** (new) — single-responsibility component that computes an owner's canonical household key (normalized last name + address). Normalization logic now lives here once.
- **`validation/HouseholdDuplicateValidator.java`** — refactored to delegate to `HouseholdKey` (no duplicated normalization) and to expose `findHouseholdMembers(...)`, with `sharesHouseholdWithExisting(...)` kept as a thin wrapper.
- **`validation/HouseholdIdGenerator.java`** (new) — derives the stable shared id deterministically from the `HouseholdKey` (`HH-` + 16 hex chars of SHA-256), so all members of a household map to the same value regardless of creation order.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — replaced `rejectDuplicateHousehold` with `applyHouseholdPolicy`, which finds household members once, rejects when not opted in, and otherwise stamps the new owner and any un-stamped existing members with the shared id.
- **`OwnerMapper.java`** — ignore `householdId` on the `OwnerFields → Owner` mapping (it's not a client-editable field); it maps automatically on `Owner → OwnerDto`.

The `householdId` derivation being deterministic makes it a genuinely stable shared identifier and keeps `b`/`c` (and the original member) consistent no matter the join order.
